In [[Abstract algebra|algebra]], a '''generic matrix ring''' is a sort of a universal [[matrix ring]].

== Definition ==
We denote by <math>F_n</math> a generic matrix ring of size ''n'' with variables <math>X_1, \dots X_m</math>. It is characterized by the universal property: given a [[commutative ring]] ''R'' and ''n''-by-''n'' [[Matrix (mathematics)|matrices]] <math>A_1, \dots, A_m</math> over ''R'', there exists a '''unique''' ring homomorphism (called the evaluation map) <math>F_n \to M_n(R)</math> extending the assignment <math>X_i \mapsto A_i</math>.

Explicitly, given a [[Field (mathematics)|field]] ''k'', it is the [[subalgebra]] <math>F_n</math> of the matrix ring <math>M_n(k[(X_l)_{ij} \mid 1 \le l \le m,\ 1 \le i, j \le n])</math> generated by ''n''-by-''n'' matrices <math>X_1, \dots, X_m</math>, where <math>(X_l)_{ij}</math> are matrix entries and commute by definition. For example, if ''m''&thinsp;=&thinsp;1 then <math>F_1</math> is a [[polynomial ring]] in one variable.

For example, a [[central polynomial]] is an element of the ring <math>F_n</math> that will map to a central element under an evaluation. (In fact, it is in the [[invariant ring]] <math>k[(X_l)_{ij}]^{\operatorname{GL}_n(k)}</math> since it is central and invariant.<ref>{{harvnb|Artin|1999|loc=Proposition V.15.2.}}</ref>)

By definition, <math>F_n</math> is a [[Quotient ring|quotient]] of the [[free ring]] <math>k\langle t_1, \dots, t_m \rangle</math> with <math>t_i \mapsto X_i</math> by the [[Ideal (ring theory)|ideal]] consisting of all ''p'' that vanish identically on all ''n''-by-''n'' matrices over ''k''.

== Geometric perspective ==
The universal property means that any ring homomorphism from <math>k\langle t_1, \dots, t_m \rangle</math> to a matrix ring factors through <math>F_n</math>. This has a following geometric meaning. In [[algebraic geometry]], the polynomial ring <math>k[t, \dots, t_m]</math> is the [[coordinate ring]] of the affine space <math>k^m</math>, and to give a point of <math>k^m</math> is to give a ring homomorphism (evaluation) <math>k[t, \dots, t_m] \to k</math> (either by [[Hilbert's Nullstellensatz]] or by the [[scheme theory]]). The free ring <math>k\langle t_1, \dots, t_m \rangle</math> plays the role of the coordinate ring of the affine space in the [[noncommutative algebraic geometry]] (i.e., we don't demand free variables to commute) and thus a generic matrix ring of size ''n'' is the coordinate ring of a noncommutative affine variety whose points are the Spec's of matrix rings of size ''n'' (see below for a more concrete discussion.)

=== The maximal spectrum of a generic matrix ring ===
{{expand section|date=June 2014}}

For simplicity, assume ''k'' is [[Algebraically closed field|algebraically closed]]. Let ''A'' be an [[Algebra over a field|algebra]] over ''k'' and let <math>\operatorname{Spec}_n(A)</math> denote the [[Set (mathematics)|set]] of all [[maximal ideal]]s <math>\mathfrak{m}</math> in ''A'' such that <math>A/\mathfrak{m} \approx M_n(k)</math>. If ''A'' is commutative, then <math>\operatorname{Spec}_1(A)</math> is the [[Glossary_of_commutative_algebra#S|maximal spectrum]] of ''A'' and <math>\operatorname{Spec}_n(A)</math> is [[Empty set|empty]] for any <math>n > 1</math>.
